findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Gradual decompression resulted in longer times to unconsciousness and death and the pharmacological interventions support the notion of a minimally negative animal experience, while providing further evidence for pain and anxiety associated with exposure to CO2.
findings.study_system: laboratory mice (experimental humane-killing welfare comparison)

findings.claim: A survey of 592 laboratory-animal professionals and researchers found attitudes to CO2 rodent euthanasia were on average ambivalent, and although 51% felt improved alternatives existed they perceived financial, institutional, regulatory, research and safety barriers to adopting these refinements.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Many participants (51%) felt that there were alternatives available that could be considered an improvement over CO2, but perceived barriers to implementing these refinements.
findings.evidence: Results. Online survey (Canada and Europe); CO2 was the most common killing method; mean attitude score ambivalent; barriers to alternatives were operational (finance, institutional culture, regulation, research, safety) rather than welfare-based.
findings.effect_size: n = 592; mean CO2 attitude 4.4 ± 1.46 on 7-point scale; 51% felt alternatives improve on CO2
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: CO2 was identified as the most common method used to kill rodents, and attitudes towards this method were variable and on average ambivalent (mean ± SD score on our 7-point scale was 4.4 ± 1.46).
findings.study_system: laboratory animal professionals and researchers (Canada/Europe survey on CO2 euthanasia)

findings.claim: An international expert meeting on laboratory animal euthanasia (Newcastle) reported there is still no consensus on which killing methods are humane for many species and developmental stages, despite an ethical and often legal imperative to minimise suffering at death.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, there is a lack of consensus regarding what methods of killing are humane for many species and stages of development.
findings.evidence: Report. International group at Newcastle University (2013) reviewed research on humane killing of mice, rats and zebrafish, factors for choosing techniques, and priorities for further research; issued recommendations to inform good practice.
findings.study_system: laboratory animal euthanasia (expert consensus meeting; mice, rats, zebrafish)

findings.claim: An experimental study of mouse euthanasia found isoflurane and sevoflurane raised catecholamine stress markers less than high-concentration CO2, suggesting volatile anaesthetics may be a lower-stress refinement, though no behavioural correlate of the difference was seen.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The rise in catecholamine concentrations suggests that CO2 exposure might be linked to a higher stress response compared to isoflurane and sevoflurane exposure, although we did not observe a behavioral correlate for that.
findings.evidence: Results. Compared CO2, isoflurane and sevoflurane in two mouse strains from gas inlet to loss of consciousness (period when animals can perceive pain/distress); adrenaline/noradrenaline increased especially with high CO2 but not with the ethers; some animals became recumbent during isoflurane/sevoflurane but not CO2.
findings.study_system: laboratory mice (NMRI, C57Bl/6J; experimental euthanasia comparison)

findings.claim: A multidisciplinary symposium convened by the Swiss Federal Food Safety and Veterinary Office concluded that, because CO2 is aversive to rodents, alternatives are urgently required and a coordinated research programme is needed to meet the need for humane killing.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A conclusion from this process was that alternatives to CO2 were urgently required, including a program of research and extension to meet the needs for humane killing of these animals.
findings.evidence: Symposium report. Brainstorming/World-Cafe process; established a large body of research shows CO2 is aversive; next step to convene international experts to draft a research strategy on CO2 alternatives.
findings.study_system: laboratory animal euthanasia (Swiss expert symposium on CO2 alternatives)

findings.claim: An experimental study applying the Rat Grimace Scale across six euthanasia methods found the inhalant isoflurane produced the highest grimace (pain) scores immediately after application, undermining the assumption that volatile anaesthetics are an unambiguous refinement over other agents.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This study aimed to evaluate pain associated with six methods of euthanasia in Wistar rats (injectable, inhalational, and physical), by applying the Rat Grimace Scale (RGS), comparing the scores, and determining the method with the highest score that might indicate pain for laboratory rodents.
findings.evidence: Results. 60 Wistar rats across pentobarbital, CO2, decapitation, isoflurane, ketamine+xylazine, ketamine+CO2; isoflurane recorded the highest grimace scores after application, attributed to pungency/muscle-relaxant effects; RGS proposed as a euthanasia-quality tool with anaesthetic limitations.
findings.effect_size: isoflurane grimace score 1.2 ± 0.20 (highest post-application)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: CO2 (0.9 ± 0.18) and isoflurane (1.2 ± 0.20) recorded the highest scores
findings.study_system: Wistar rats (experimental Rat Grimace Scale evaluation of euthanasia methods)

findings.claim: A philosophical analysis argues the 3Rs are not truly anthropocentric but arose from an animal-centred ethic constrained by a cooperation strategy that had to accept research purposes as given, and that governments should therefore also target animal-free question-selection, not only humane method-selection.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In fact, the 3Rs prioritize research purposes even more strongly than an ethical anthropocentrist would.
findings.evidence: Argument. Drawing on UFAW founder Charles Hume (who employed Russell and Burch), shows the 3Rs' narrow focus on humane method selection stems from an organizational strategy seeking voluntary researcher cooperation; implies protecting animals for their own sake requires state action on question selection.
findings.study_system: animal research ethics (philosophical analysis of the 3Rs)

findings.claim: A contractarian analysis argues, against Rawls, that some animals may possess the 'moral powers' constituting moral personality (a sense of the good and of justice), so a Rawlsian theory of justice should not exclude them a priori.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Contrary to Rawls's assumptions, it appears that some animals may possess the moral powers that comprise moral personality, albeit to a lesser extent than most humans.
findings.evidence: Argument. Cites inequity aversion and social play as evidence some animals have a sense of justice within their social groups; concludes the range-property concept of moral personality may need reconsideration to include such animals.
findings.study_system: animal moral status / contractarian ethics (philosophical analysis)

findings.claim: Qualitative interviews with UK Named Veterinary Surgeons found the 'openness' agenda in animal research can create tensions for those responsible for welfare, who may need to voice ambivalence or concern about their own role, arguing for a culture of dialogue rather than one-way transparency.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Overall, this social scientific analysis reveals that the current openness agenda has the potential to create tensions for professionals, as they seek to manage regulatory and public imaginaries of the veterinary identity alongside the animal research controversy.
findings.evidence: Qualitative study. NVS practise, avoid and challenge openness; paper calls for openness that allows welfare-responsible staff to express concern, and for sustained study of veterinary-society relations in contested practices where care and harm coincide.
findings.study_system: UK Named Veterinary Surgeons (qualitative interviews on openness/culture of care)

findings.claim: An exploratory survey of 503 experts in Germany concluded that a Culture of Care has not yet been fully established in animal-research institutions, despite decades of 3Rs implementation and the concept being promoted since 2002.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The results allow for the initial conclusion that a Culture of Care has not been fully established yet.
findings.evidence: Results. 503 experts surveyed with closed (five-point agreement) and open questions on perceptions and institutional implementation of Culture of Care; authors call for holistic, critical, interdisciplinary culture centred on the animals' perspective.
findings.effect_size: 503 experts surveyed
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In the present project, 503 experts in Germany were exploratively surveyed about their individual perceptions of Culture of Care and its implementation within their institutions.
findings.study_system: German animal-research experts (survey on Culture of Care implementation)

findings.claim: A survey of 288 medical graduate students found relatively low awareness of laboratory animal welfare and limited related knowledge, with awareness dipping during the COVID-19 pandemic, pointing to a gap in 3Rs education in medical schools.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We found that medical graduate students showed relatively low awareness of laboratory animal welfare and limited understanding of related knowledge.
findings.evidence: Results. Survey of 288 students (2019-2023 cohorts) via a compulsory course exam; basic-medicine and female students showed higher awareness; awareness rising over years but decreased during COVID-19; recommends strengthening welfare/3Rs education.
findings.effect_size: n = 288 medical graduate students
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: To investigate the knowledge and attitudes of medical graduate students regarding laboratory animal welfare, a survey was conducted on 288 medical graduate students from the 2019 to 2023 cohorts through the final exam of the compulsory course 'Medical Laboratory Animal Science.'
findings.study_system: medical graduate students (survey of laboratory-animal-welfare awareness)

findings.claim: A FELASA Working Group produced learning outcomes and a template curriculum for teaching experimental design to scientists using animals, framing better design education as a means to reduce animal use and address concerns about study conduct.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Good education and training for scientists undertaking animal experiments is important for providing understanding of key issues in experimental design (ED) and for alleviating continuing concerns about the conduct of animal and in vitro research studies.
findings.evidence: Working-group output. Provides learning outcomes for early-career researchers, a 16-hour (12h tuition) 2-day workshop template, running guidance, a glossary and a train-the-trainers programme; two trial workshops showed effective learning at immediate and one-year follow-up.
findings.study_system: laboratory animal science education (FELASA experimental-design teaching)

findings.claim: A scoping review identified only 17 resources to guide harm-benefit analysis for animal protocols and concluded that deliberation among ethics-committee members should be favoured over scoring approaches, and case-by-case decisions over a false ideal of accuracy.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Decision-making based on deliberation among committee members should be supported over the use of scoring approaches.
findings.evidence: Results. Systematic search (PubMed/Scopus/WoS, Europe and North America, 1985-2023); 17 HBA decision resources found, variously using mathematical calculation, discussion guidelines or combinations; concludes case-by-case deliberation is preferable to scoring accuracy that is not realistically practicable.
findings.effect_size: 17 HBA decision resources identified
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: 17 resources that can guide HBA and decision-making were identified.
findings.study_system: harm-benefit analysis decision tools (scoping review, Europe/North America)

findings.claim: Arguing the classic 3Rs are limited for guiding ethical management of animal experimentation, ethnopharmacology researchers propose a '4R' framework adding Responsibility to encapsulate researchers' accountability and cross-species empathy.
findings.claim_source_sentence: To address these gaps, the field has introduced the 4R principles, which expand the original framework by adding "Responsibility."
findings.evidence: Framework paper. Details Reduction (efficient designs, tissue banks, better modelling success), Refinement (less distress, non/minimally-invasive techniques), Replacement (in vitro, 3D organoids, deep learning) and Responsibility (regulation, ethics training, welfare awareness).
findings.study_system: ethnopharmacology animal research ethics (4R framework proposal)

findings.claim: A German study of early-career researchers argues that the distress, poor working conditions and unresolved 3Rs dilemmas they face in animal experiments jeopardise both animal and researcher wellbeing and undermine scientific quality, potentially driving ECRs out of academia.
findings.claim_source_sentence: These challenges not only jeopardize the well-being of both animals and researchers, but also undermine the quality of scientific work, potentially driving ECRs out of academia.
findings.evidence: Mixed methods (ECR survey plus expert workshop). Recommends better communication, recognising cultural differences, peer coaching/mentoring and stronger institutional support as a culture-of-care strategy harmonising scientific progress with ethics.
findings.study_system: early-career animal researchers in Germany (culture of care; mixed methods)

findings.claim: A longitudinal study of first-year veterinary students found an introductory laboratory-animal-science lecture significantly increased compassion toward laboratory animals, but also slightly lowered some anti-compassion scores in a way suggesting early formation of a professional utilitarian outlook.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A pre- and post-lecture survey revealed a significant increase in total compassion scores.
findings.evidence: Results. Compassion gains largest in students with prior pet ownership and no animal-protection experience, notably for attitudes to natural behaviours and legal regulation; a slight decrease in some anti-compassion items indicates emerging professional utilitarian perspective; frames foundational education as building a culture of care.
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: A slight decrease in some anti-compassion item scores was also observed, potentially indicating the early formation of a professional utilitarian perspective.
findings.study_system: first-year veterinary students (pre-post compassion survey)

findings.claim: An audit of the animal subarachnoid-haemorrhage literature found 40% of 608 studies had image-related problems yet only about a quarter had been corrected, indicating stalled scientific self-correction that wastes animals and misleads future research.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We included 608 articles, of which 243 articles were identified as problematic (40.0%).
findings.evidence: Results. Of 243 problematic articles only 55 (22.6%) corrected, 19 (7.8%) retracted, and in 16.4% of corrected papers problems persisted; 87.7% of problematic articles had a corresponding author from a Chinese institute; concludes self-correction has stalled in this field.
findings.effect_size: 243 of 608 problematic (40.0%); 19 (7.8%) retracted; 213 (87.7%) China-affiliated
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Of the 243 problematic articles, 55 (22.6%) have been corrected, 7 (2.9%) have received an expression of concern, 5 (2.1%) were marked with the Taylor & Francis under investigation pop-up, and 19 (7.8%) were retracted.
findings.study_system: animal subarachnoid-haemorrhage studies (image-integrity audit)

findings.claim: An IACUC-focused analysis argues committees operate under an 'ethics of uncertainty' because knowledge of effective analgesia is incomplete and fears about analgesic effects on data push scientists to withhold pain relief, and concludes this should shift IACUCs toward greater caution about permitting painful experiments.
findings.claim_source_sentence: I conclude that applying current animal pain management knowledge to prevailing ethical principles will shift IACUC toward greater caution in allowing potentially painful animal experiments, with heightened caution regarding the ability of analgesics to mitigate the animals' pain.
findings.evidence: Argument. Highlights limits of veterinary 'professional judgment' when a model's pain and analgesic efficacy are unknown, the review of Category E (unalleviated pain) studies, and the harm-benefit balance; incomplete analgesic knowledge across sexes/ages/genotypes undermines refinement.
findings.study_system: laboratory rodent analgesia / IACUC review (ethical analysis)

findings.claim: A commentary highlights a regulatory contradiction: in the EU, breeding immunodeficient mice is classed and permitted as a painful experiment even when established severity-assessment methods detect no pain, suffering or harm, and calls for individualised severity analysis instead.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, the breeding of immunodeficient mice is considered an experiment requiring a permit, even if no pain, suffering or harm is observed under scientifically required defined hygienic housing conditions, as determined by established methods of severity assessment.
findings.evidence: Commentary. Notes that in the EU breeding genetically modified animals is by definition an experiment if offspring may suffer; argues the blanket treatment of immunodeficient lines is contradictory and proposes individualised severity assessment and approval procedures.
findings.study_system: genetically modified / immunodeficient mice (severity assessment; regulatory commentary)

findings.claim: A practical guideline argues that harm assessment for genetically altered animals is uniquely difficult because it is often impossible to predict prospectively what harm, if any, the animals will experience, complicating the prospective harm-benefit analysis required by EU law.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A unique challenge when using GA lines is the significant lack of knowledge in this context, making it difficult and sometimes impossible to estimate harm prospectively with sufficient certainty, since it is not predictable what sort of harm-if at all-the animals are going to experience.
findings.evidence: Guideline. EU Directive 2010/63/EU requires prospective harm-benefit weighing; GA lines raise new issues because harms are unpredictable; presents guidance on relevant harm factors and handling uncertainty in the HBA and welfare assessment.
findings.study_system: genetically altered animals (harm/welfare assessment guideline, EU)

findings.claim: Researchers developed and validated bioinformatics-based composite measure schemes that allow evidence-based, individualised severity classification of adult and young mice and direct comparison across induced and genetic disease models, providing a tool to validate refinement measures.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In conclusion, the bioinformatics approach confirmed the suitability of the composite measure schemes for evidence-based comparative severity assessment in adult and young mice.
findings.evidence: Results. Composite schemes of behavioural and biochemical parameters built from published datasets; ROC and PCA/k-means clustering confirmed severity-level separation; an R package is released to apply the approach and validate refinements.
findings.study_system: laboratory mice (bioinformatics-based severity assessment tool)

findings.claim: German laboratory-animal facility managers argue for extending the 3Rs to '6 Rs' (adding respect, responsibility and reproducibility) and describe concrete culture-of-care measures such as no-blame incident reporting (CIRS-LAS) to protect both animals and staff.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The 6 Rs must be considered at all times: replacement, reduction, refinement, respect, responsibility, and reproducibility.
findings.evidence: Perspective. Managers face constant conflict between scientific necessity, care and harm; recommended measures include improved housing, uniform handling, quality-management structures, a no-blame Critical Incident Reporting System (CIRS-LAS) and open communication with public and authorities.
findings.study_system: laboratory animal facilities in Germany (culture of care; management perspective)

findings.claim: Noting that most of the 5,784 primates used for science in Europe are macaques, the PWIN project argues a comprehensive, species-specific lifelong welfare-assessment tool for research macaques is still lacking and adapts a farm-animal protocol to fill the gap.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In Europe, the majority of the 5,784 primates currently used for scientific purposes are macaques (Macaca fascicularis and M. mulatta).
findings.evidence: Project description. PWIN adapts the AWIN farm-animal protocol to macaques, combining housing/nutrition/health/behaviour evaluation with 10-minute continuous focal sampling, to give repeated lifelong welfare assessment before, during and after procedures and support 3Rs-aligned, transparent authorisation.
findings.effect_size: 5,784 primates used for scientific purposes in Europe
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In Europe, the majority of the 5,784 primates currently used for scientific purposes are macaques (Macaca fascicularis and M. mulatta).
findings.study_system: research macaques in Europe (welfare-indicator tool development)

findings.claim: The largest international survey of nonhuman-primate behavioural management (49 facilities, 50,842 NHPs) found large regional variation, with UK and EU facilities generally ahead of the US on social housing and enrichment, showing perceived constraints on welfare-improving practices can be overcome.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The findings suggest large variation in NHP behavioral management practices between world regions.
findings.evidence: Results. Survey (2019-2020) of EU/UK/US facilities; UK/EU led on social housing proportions, later infant weaning, pen enclosures, above-minimum floor space and destructible enrichment; comparisons with 2003/2014 US surveys show progress; concludes constraints can be overcome with knowledge transfer and resources.
findings.effect_size: 49 facilities; 50,842 NHPs
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Most respondents reported the number of NHPs at their institutions, which totaled 50,842.
findings.study_system: nonhuman primate research facilities (EU/UK/US behavioural-management survey)

findings.claim: Beauchamp and DeGrazia argue the 1959 3Rs are an insufficient ethical framework and propose six principles (three of social benefit, three of animal welfare) that they contend better bridge the divide between the animal-research and animal-protection communities.
findings.claim_source_sentence: These six principles, we argue, constitute a more suitable framework than any other that is currently available, including the canonical 3 Rs advanced in 1959 by William M. S. Russell and Rex L. Burch.
findings.evidence: Framework paper. Justifies a new framework on six recent developments; argues common ground exists in the core values of social benefit and animal welfare; presents three social-benefit and three animal-welfare principles as superior to the 3Rs.
findings.study_system: animal research ethics (Beauchamp-DeGrazia principles framework)

findings.claim: Assessing ethical and regulatory protocols for non-human-primate research across 13 countries, the authors argue that diversity in national regulation is often mistaken for the absence of common international welfare standards, and build a resource to support cross-border collaboration.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Diversity in regulation of animal research is sometimes mistaken for the absence of common international welfare standards.
findings.evidence: Resource paper. Reviewed NHP welfare/regulatory frameworks for 13 countries in Asia, Europe and North America with a neuroscience focus; produced a tabulated resource to enable evidence-based, solution-oriented discussion and inform the public and stakeholders.
findings.effect_size: 13 countries with NHP research guidelines assessed
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Here, the ethical and regulatory protocols for 13 countries that have guidelines in place for biomedical research involving NHPs were assessed with a focus on neuroscience.
findings.study_system: non-human primate neuroscience regulation (13-country comparative resource)

findings.claim: A comparative review of neurogenesis argues non-human primates, especially monkeys, are valuable models with closer neural resemblance to humans than rodents, while cautioning about the impacts and limitations of NHP models for neurogenesis research.
findings.claim_source_sentence: While non-human primates, especially monkeys, serve as valuable models with closer neural resemblance to humans, we highlight the potential impacts and limitations of non-human primate models on both physiological and pathological neurogenesis research.
findings.evidence: Review. Compares neurogenesis across rodents, non-human primates and humans from embryonic development to adulthood, emphasising conservation and species diversity enabled by single-cell multiomics and gene editing.
findings.study_system: neurogenesis models (rodents vs non-human primates vs humans; review)

findings.claim: Analysis of Swedish animal-research ethics applications found harm, benefit and 3Rs information often insufficient or missing, with non-technical summaries frequently describing the 3Rs poorly or confusing them.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, amongst the NTS analyzed in our study, the 3Rs were, to varying degrees, insufficiently or not at all described, and one third of the NTSs displayed some mix-up between them.
findings.evidence: Results/Discussion. Empirical audit of applications to Swedish Animal Ethics Committees; information needed for a harm-benefit analysis routinely absent; authors propose nine action points.
findings.effect_size: one third of NTSs mixed up the 3Rs; only 59% of researchers believed their research achieved its goals
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: recent figures show that, in hindsight, only 59% of questioned researchers in Sweden believe that their research did in fact achieve its goals
findings.study_system: animal-research ethical review applications, Sweden (Animal Ethics Committees; Directive 2010/63/EU)

findings.claim: A systematic review of 65 documents found the most prevalent barrier to communicating animal research is that the research itself poses risks and harms to animals, appearing in 86% of documents.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In total, 56 out of 65 documents (86%) address how research is not well suited for science communication because it poses risks and causes harm to test animals (71%), is highly complex and involves uncertainties (63%), or may have legitimacy problems (54%).
findings.evidence: Results. Qualitative content analysis of 65 documents; seven barrier themes; harm to animals (71%), complexity (63%) and legitimacy (54%) are leading sub-barriers.
findings.effect_size: 56/65 documents (86%); harm 71%; complexity 63%; legitimacy 54%
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In total, 56 out of 65 documents (86%) address how research is not well suited for science communication because it poses risks and causes harm to test animals (71%), is highly complex and involves uncertainties (63%), or may have legitimacy problems (54%).
findings.study_system: systematic literature review of science-communication barriers on animal experimentation (65 documents)

findings.claim: FELASA fish-killing recommendations note that commonly used anaesthetics such as tricaine induce aversive behaviour in fish, so humane killing forces a trade-off between a fast but aversive protocol and a slow but peaceful one.
findings.claim_source_sentence: For instance, there is evidence that the commonly used anaesthetic tricaine induces aversive behaviour in several fish species.
findings.evidence: Body. FELASA working-group recommendations for humane killing of laboratory fish; introduces the concept of ideal euthanasia and the dilemma of prompt-but-stressful vs slow-but-stress-free death.
findings.study_system: laboratory fish euthanasia (FELASA working group; zebrafish and other species)

findings.claim: Only 6 of 30 European countries examined have produced guidance documents to support harm-benefit analysis, leaving reviewing bodies with sparse, inconsistent guidance; the authors build a compound HBA model to fill the gap.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Indeed, only 6 of the 30 European countries investigated have produced GDs to support HBAs during project evaluation ().
findings.evidence: Introduction/Methods. HBA guidance is fragmentary; the compound model merges 'discourse' and 'metric' model elements into a transparent, practice-oriented decision tool meeting Directive requirements.
findings.effect_size: 6 of 30 European countries produced HBA guidance documents
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Indeed, only 6 of the 30 European countries investigated have produced GDs to support HBAs during project evaluation ().
findings.study_system: harm-benefit analysis guidance across European countries (Directive 2010/63/EU project evaluation)

findings.claim: The paper documents that Russell and Burch's 3Rs framework rests on a welfarist premise, articulated by their supervisor Charles Hume, that painless killing is not a harm, so animal death is largely omitted from 3Rs-based regulation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: their employer and supervisor, Charles W. Hume, explicitly endorsed a welfarist view of animal death, stating: “There is no harm in killing animals provided it be done painlessly”
findings.evidence: Body. Distinguishes four classes of research killing (during, before, 'surplus', 'leftover'); argues regulations reduce surplus but neglect that death itself can be a morally relevant harm.
findings.study_system: animal research ethics (moral status of animal death; philosophical foundations of the 3Rs)

findings.claim: The Polish Zebrafish Society argues that broad adoption of zebrafish models supports the 3Rs and can substantially reduce reliance on higher vertebrate models.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Broad adoption of zebrafish-based approaches can accelerate preclinical discovery, enhance translational relevance, and substantially reduce reliance on higher vertebrate models.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Field-specific recommendations positioning zebrafish as a replacement/reduction model across oncology, toxicology, neurology and other domains.
findings.study_system: zebrafish (Danio rerio) as biomedical model supporting the 3Rs

findings.claim: A multinational group argues that despite broad acceptance, interpretations of the 3Rs vary substantially and shape statutory frameworks with both technical and practical impacts.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Despite their broad acceptance, interpretations of the 3Rs vary substantially, shaping statutory frameworks at various levels, with both technical and practical impacts.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Calls for a common interpretation of Replacement, Reduction and Refinement to reduce divergence across policy and legislation.
findings.study_system: 3Rs principles interpretation (international consensus paper)

findings.claim: A bibliometric review finds NAMs publications rose steeply since 2015 and that toxicology's ethical discourse is shifting from 'symbolic' ethics toward embedded, actionable frameworks including a fourth R (responsibility).
findings.claim_source_sentence: Our findings reveal a steep increase in NAMs publications since 2015, with in vitro and in silico approaches at the forefront.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Mixed-methods bibliometric mapping of ethics and sustainability in NAMs-related toxicology; identifies a move from symbolic to operational ethics.
findings.effect_size: steep increase in NAMs publications since 2015
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Our findings reveal a steep increase in NAMs publications since 2015, with in vitro and in silico approaches at the forefront.
findings.study_system: toxicology new approach methodologies (bibliometric analysis and review)

findings.claim: A 3Rs review advocates partial replacement with less sentient animals (C. elegans, Drosophila, zebrafish embryos) alongside refinement to reduce animal numbers and severity in muscle-disease research.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Where this is not possible, a 3Rs approach advocates partial replacement with the use of less sentient animals (including invertebrates (such as worms Caenorhabditis elegans and fruit flies Drosophila melanogaster) and embryonic stages of small vertebrates such as the zebrafish Danio rerio) alongside refinement of experimental design and improved research practices to reduce the numbers of animals used and the severity of their experience.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Reviews cell-culture, tissue-engineered and less-sentient-animal alternatives for muscle development and inherited myopathy research.
findings.study_system: muscle development/myopathy models (replacement and reduction alternatives)

findings.claim: The last decade has seen rising public interest in decapod crustacean welfare and statutory legal protection introduced in several countries, extending research-animal protection to aquatic invertebrates.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, in the last decade many parts of the world have seen an increase in public interest in the welfare of decapod crustaceans and statutory legal protection has been introduced in several countries.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Horizon paper on including decapods in scientific-use legislation; existing vertebrate-oriented rules may be unsuitable for aquatic invertebrates.
findings.study_system: decapod crustaceans (sentience, legislation, 3Rs)

findings.claim: Zebrafish account for approximately 50% of laboratory fish in Europe; the study developed a group electro-euthanasia method delivered through the housing water to refine killing of large stocks.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Zebrafish are widely used in research, accounting for approximately 50% of all laboratory fish across Europe.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Portable plate electrodes euthanised adult zebrafish in groups in standard 3.5-8 L aquaria; proposed as a practical refinement for colony management.
findings.effect_size: approximately 50% of all laboratory fish across Europe
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Zebrafish are widely used in research, accounting for approximately 50% of all laboratory fish across Europe.
findings.study_system: zebrafish euthanasia (electrical stunning in housing aquaria)

findings.claim: Preclinical systematic reviews aim to evaluate whether existing animal data are solid enough to translate to trials or to highlight gaps, thereby justifying or obviating new animal studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: One of the main goals of preclinical SRs is to identify aspiring treatment strategies and evaluate if currently available data is solid enough to translate to clinical trials or highlight the gaps, thus justifying the need for new studies.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Narrative review on rigorous preclinical systematic reviews/meta-analyses as an evidence-synthesis and reduction tool, with pediatric-specific considerations.
findings.study_system: preclinical systematic reviews/meta-analyses (evidence synthesis; Reduction)

findings.claim: An automated living evidence tool (AD-SOLES) summarises in vivo Alzheimer's evidence to reduce research waste and highlight knowledge gaps.
findings.claim_source_sentence: AD-SOLES aims to offer guidance for research improvement, reduce research waste, highlight knowledge gaps, and support informed decision making for researchers, funders, patients, and the public.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Automated collection, curation and visualisation of in vivo AD experiments to accelerate evidence synthesis and reduce duplication/waste.
findings.study_system: automated evidence synthesis for in vivo Alzheimer's research (Reduction/research waste)

findings.claim: Pre-registering animal systematic review protocols avoids unplanned duplication of reviews and reduces reporting biases.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Pre-registering a systematic review protocol has several benefits, including avoiding unplanned duplication of reviews, reducing reporting biases, and providing structure throughout the review process.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Ten practical tips for pre-registering preclinical systematic reviews on PROSPERO4animals to reduce bias and duplication.
findings.study_system: preclinical systematic review pre-registration (PROSPERO4animals)

findings.claim: Organ-on-chip models promise to reduce dependence on animal models but require clear criteria for the evidence standards needed to replace animals, among other ethical challenges.
findings.claim_source_sentence: OoCs promise to enhance drug discovery, reduce dependence on animal models, and enable personalized treatments.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Mapping review of OoC ethics identifies nine themes including animal experimentation and the need for evidence standards to justify replacing animal models.
findings.study_system: organ-on-chip replacement models (ethics mapping review)

findings.claim: The FDA roadmap to reduce animal testing frames conventional preclinical safety assessment as suffering from poor translational predictability, high cost, ethical concerns and interspecies differences, motivating a shift to NAMs.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The aim is to address the longstanding challenges of conventional preclinical safety assessment using animal models, including poor translational predictability, high cost, ethical concerns, and inherent interspecies biological differences, resulting in high clinical attrition and delayed access to effective therapies.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Commentary evaluating the FDA's first-year progress toward human-centric NAMs (organoids, organ-on-chip, in silico, AI) in nonclinical safety assessment.
findings.study_system: FDA NAMs roadmap (replacement in drug safety assessment)

findings.claim: The authors propose a three-step approach (agree a welfare definition, then a framework, then build validated tools) but note this has not always been followed for existing welfare assessment tools.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, this three-step approach has not always been followed in the development of welfare assessment tools currently in use.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Review arguing that transparent definitions and frameworks are prerequisites for reliable, convergent welfare assessment tools.
findings.study_system: animal welfare assessment tool development (definitions and frameworks)

findings.claim: Organoid technology raises ethical questions (donor consent, commercial use, 'potential life') that vary by application and require tailored ethical-review guidelines.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Each field of science and technology presents specific ethical questions regarding its application; risks, benefits, and monitoring procedures vary, thus requiring tailored review guidelines.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Systematic review of ethical-review considerations for organoid applications, spanning consent, moral status and governance.
findings.study_system: organoid models (ethical review; replacement)

findings.claim: Patients, despite their high stake in biomedical research, are rarely heard in animal-research policy debates; the authors argue for an all-inclusive democratic engagement approach.
findings.claim_source_sentence: However, their perspectives are rarely heard in policy-related discussions on animal experiments.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Essay on inclusive, democratic animal-research policy that actively involves patients alongside pro- and anti-research stakeholders.
findings.study_system: animal research policy and public/patient engagement

findings.claim: An open-source, low-cost limited-bedding-and-nesting apparatus is offered to standardise a chronic early-life-stress mouse model, improving reproducibility while supporting pup survival.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Here, we provide standardized guidelines for a cost-effective open-source mouse LBN apparatus design, which could further enhance the model's utility while supporting pup survival.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Standardised open-source LBN design plus characterisation of maternal/pup stress markers; addresses cross-study variability in ELS models.
findings.effect_size: at PND 10 pups showed reduced corticosterone and lower body weight vs controls
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: At PND 10, pups exhibit significantly reduced blood serum corticosterone levels and lower body weight compared with those reared under control conditions.
findings.study_system: mouse early-life stress model (limited bedding/nesting; standardisation/reproducibility)

findings.claim: Refined antibiotic-cocktail regimens generate pseudo-germ-free mice with effective bacterial clearance while minimising toxicity, reducing weight loss and mortality.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Optimized antibiotic regimens achieved substantial bacterial depletion while reducing weight loss and mortality.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Refinement of pseudo-germ-free mouse models by adjusting antibiotic concentrations and adding sweeteners to reduce adverse effects.
findings.study_system: pseudo-germ-free mouse model (refinement of antibiotic regimens)

findings.claim: Male-only nonclinical study designs generate surpluses of unused female animals in breeding colonies, undermining the 3Rs, particularly Reduction, at the project or facility level.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Sex bias is also an animal welfare concern: male-only strategies can generate surpluses of unused females in breeding colonies, challenging the 3Rs-particularly Reduction-when evaluated at the project or facility level.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Review integrating scientific rigor, welfare and regulation to argue for sex-aware nonclinical designs (SABV) that also serve Reduction.
findings.study_system: nonclinical study design (sex as a biological variable; Reduction/surplus animals)

findings.claim: Anthropocentric digital interfaces in animal cognition research may impair data quality and welfare; a bottom-up biocentric design centred on animals' behaviour is proposed for more ethically sound research.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This approach presents potential limitations regarding data quality and its impact on participants, caregivers, and researchers alike.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Advocates biocentric, iterative-design test apparatuses that fit the animal rather than fitting animals to human-centred technology.
findings.study_system: animal cognition research interfaces (biocentric/refinement design)

findings.claim: Two Belgian institutions built a shared severity classification because Directive guidance is often lacking or too vague, which can cause inconsistent classification between and within countries and institutions.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This, in turn, may lead to inconsistencies in severity classification between countries, within countries and even within institutions.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Procedures grouped into 16 (sub)categories with well-defined cut-offs; primarily prospective but usable for actual severity assessment.
findings.effect_size: 16 (sub)categories of procedures
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: This work started with listing all in-house procedures and assigning them to 16 (sub)categories.
findings.study_system: laboratory animal procedure severity classification (Belgium; Directive 2010/63)

findings.claim: Published welfare score sheets often contain fundamental flaws or are setting-specific; the authors propose an eight-step procedure to design an adaptable score sheet for (retrospective) severity assessment.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Several score sheet examples have been published; however, some contain fundamental flaws or are designed for specific settings only, requiring modifications to fit other experimental designs.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Eight essential steps for designing an experiment-specific score sheet supporting monitoring and retrospective severity assessment under the 3Rs.
findings.study_system: welfare score-sheet design (severity assessment; 3Rs)

findings.claim: A multivariate composite (RELSA) severity score is more robust than single readouts, but individual distress scores are model-dependent and prone to experimental variation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: It was found that the performance of the readout parameters is model-dependent and that the distress score is prone to experimental variation.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Bootstrapped analysis of body weight, burrowing, nesting and distress score across four GI models; RELSA combines parameters into a robust quantitative severity estimate.
findings.study_system: gastrointestinal mouse models (evidence-based severity assessment; RELSA composite score)

findings.claim: A pilot analysis of 18 Swedish ethical-review applications found a majority of Animal Ethics Committee decisions failed to include the legally required harm-benefit analysis and none documented a 3Rs evaluation.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Similarly, no Animal Ethics Committee decision contained any account of evaluation of the 3Rs and a majority failed to include harm-benefit analysis as required by law.
findings.evidence: Abstract. In-depth analysis of 18 applications/decisions; structural mismatch between legislation and forms leaves information incomplete by design, undermining HBA and transparency.
findings.effect_size: 18 applications; majority of AEC decisions lacked HBA; none documented 3Rs
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Through in-depth analysis of 18 applications and decisions of ethical reviews, we found that there are recurring problems within the ethical review process in Sweden.
findings.study_system: ethical review process, Sweden (Directive 2010/63; HBA/3Rs compliance)

findings.claim: In a 3x3 multi-laboratory reproducibility test of ecological insect-behaviour studies, the direction/significance of treatment effects was far more reproducible than the effect sizes, mirroring the reproducibility problems previously documented in rodent research.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We were able to reproduce the overall statistical significance of the treatment effect in 83% of the replicate experiments; however, reproducing the overall effect size was successful in only 66%, while both criteria were achieved in 58% of cases.
findings.evidence: Multi-laboratory (3 sites x 3 insect species) reproducibility experiment using random-effect meta-analysis.
findings.effect_size: 83% of replicates reproduced statistical significance; 66% reproduced effect size; 58% reproduced both
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: We were able to reproduce the overall statistical significance of the treatment effect in 83% of the replicate experiments; however, reproducing the overall effect size was successful in only 66%, while both criteria were achieved in 58% of cases.
findings.study_system: Insects (turnip sawfly, meadow grasshopper, red flour beetle); 3x3 multi-laboratory design

findings.claim: A single-laboratory 'mini-experiment' design that splits a study across several time points improved reproducibility in about half of tested treatment effects without increasing the total number of animals used.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In line with this, our study demonstrate that the mini-experiment design led to more reproducible results compared to the conventionally standardised design in about half of all investigated treatment effects, even though the total number of animals used was identical.
findings.evidence: Four conventional vs four mini-experiment replicate experiments across four mouse strains over 1.5 years.
findings.effect_size: significantly lower between-replicate variation in 3 of 6 strain comparisons; identical total animal numbers
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: More precisely, improved reproducibility was reflected by a significantly lower between-replicate experiment variation in three out of six strain comparisons.
findings.study_system: Mice (four inbred strains); single-laboratory mini-experiment vs conventional design

findings.claim: A six-laboratory experiment found that a simple form of population heterogenization increased within-experiment variation but was too weak to overcome the large between-laboratory variation, so standardization alone does not guarantee reproducibility.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Although heterogenization significantly increased within-experiment variation relative to between-experiment variation, the effect was too weak to account for the large variation between laboratories and improve reproducibility substantially.
findings.evidence: Six laboratories each tested 64 female mice of two inbred strains across five behavioral tests under standardized vs heterogenized designs.
findings.effect_size: 6 laboratories x 64 mice each; heterogenization effect too weak vs between-lab variation
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Each of six laboratories used 64 female mice of two inbred strains (C57BL6NCrl, DBA/2NCrl, n = 32 each) and examined them for strain differences in five commonly used behavioral tests (barrier test, vertical pole test, elevated zero maze, open field test, novel object test).
findings.study_system: Mice (C57BL/6NCrl, DBA/2NCrl); six-laboratory behavioural study

findings.claim: Machine-learning (NLP) classifiers were trained on thousands of full-text animal-experiment publications to automatically detect reporting of risk-of-bias measures, enabling large-scale monitoring of methodological quality.
findings.claim_source_sentence: After removing invalid records (for instance where text conversion failed), 7840 full‐text publications had annotations for random allocation, blinded assessment of outcome and animal exclusions, and 7089 had annotations for conflict of interests and animal welfare regulations.
findings.evidence: Supervised NLP models (CNN, RNN, BERT) trained on annotated full-text animal-study corpus.
findings.effect_size: 7840 full-text publications annotated for random allocation/blinding/exclusions; 7089 for conflict-of-interest/welfare
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: After removing invalid records (for instance where text conversion failed), 7840 full‐text publications had annotations for random allocation, blinded assessment of outcome and animal exclusions, and 7089 had annotations for conflict of interests and animal welfare regulations.
findings.study_system: 7840 animal-experiment publications; NLP risk-of-bias classifiers

findings.claim: A retrospective analysis of a rat liver-cirrhosis surgery model optimized welfare score-sheet cut-off values to better predict death and avoid unnecessary euthanasia, with the humane endpoint set at a score above 20.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In general, scores exceeding 20 were defined as the humane endpoint, and animals were euthanased immediately.
findings.evidence: Retrospective ROC analysis of a semi-quantitative score-sheet in a bile-duct-ligation cohort.
findings.effect_size: 89 rats (47 bile-duct-ligation, 42 sham); humane endpoint defined at score > 20
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The entire study cohort comprised 89 animals, including 47 rats subjected to BDL and 42 to sham surgery ().
findings.study_system: Male Sprague Dawley rats; bile-duct-ligation liver cirrhosis surgery; retrospective severity score-sheet

findings.claim: A refined visible-implant-elastomer tagging protocol for zebrafish, adding lidocaine analgesia and antiseptic after-treatment, reduced the high mortality and poor tag retention of the original protocol.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Even with the use of a standard recommended dose of MS-222 (130–140 mg/L) for anaesthesia, we observed a high daily mortality rate (20–25%).
findings.evidence: Iterative refinement of anaesthesia/analgesia and tagging materials across zebrafish populations.
findings.effect_size: initial daily mortality 20–25% with standard MS-222; tag retention improved from 60–70% to 85–90% after removing curing agent
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: After eliminating the use of the curing agent (hardener) for the slightly changed “advanced” base protocol, tag retention rates immediately improved from 60–70% to 85–90% (~100–170 individuals lost some portion of their tags) ().
findings.study_system: Zebrafish (Danio rerio); VIE tagging refinement with lidocaine analgesia

findings.claim: A practical guide on Reduction argues that optimal reduction is not using as few animals as possible but calculating the 'right number', warning that excessive reduction produces underpowered, unreliable studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We will discuss study planning, ways to calculate the minimum number of animals needed for a study, the danger of trying to reduce too much, and finally, how to calculate the right number of animals needed.
findings.evidence: Methodological review of experimental design and sample-size calculation for animal studies.
findings.study_system: Review; experimental design and sample-size calculation for animal experimentation (Reduction)

findings.claim: The scientific and legal recognition of animal sentience since the 1990s has produced a radical shift in the moral status accorded to laboratory animals and in how their welfare is protected.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The recognition of sentience in animals from the 1990s onwards has thus effected a radical shift in the way we view the moral status of animals and how we provide for and ensure their welfare.
findings.evidence: Conceptual analysis of the 'sentience shift' in animal research regulation and practice.
findings.study_system: Ethics/philosophy analysis; animal sentience, moral status, laboratory animal welfare

findings.claim: Even as cephalopods gain welfare recognition, there is no established humane, commercially practical slaughter method, leaving a key welfare evidence gap for these animals.
findings.claim_source_sentence: There is currently an evidence gap regarding humane slaughter methods that are commercially practical and available.
findings.evidence: Review of commercial practices (farming, capture, transport, slaughter) affecting cephalopod and decapod welfare.
findings.study_system: Cephalopod molluscs and decapod crustaceans; commercial welfare practices

findings.claim: A comprehensive behavioural/biochemical severity analysis concluded that an electrical kindling epilepsy paradigm in rats causes only a longer-lasting mild impact and should be classified as moderate severity.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The findings argue against a persistent level of pronounced distress and suggest a classification of the kindling paradigm as a model with moderate severity based on a longer-lasting mild impact on animal behavioral patterns.
findings.evidence: Evidence-based severity assessment using nest scoring, anxiety tests and corticosterone metrics.
findings.study_system: Rats; electrical kindling epilepsy model; evidence-based severity assessment

findings.claim: A porcine-adapted surgical Apgar score was piloted as an objective perioperative risk/refinement tool in laboratory animal science, where such clinical scoring systems are rarely used.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Within this pilot study, we could demonstrate the usefulness of the modified SAS (pSAS) in a porcine kidney transplantation model.
findings.evidence: Pilot in vivo application of a species-adapted surgical Apgar score plus literature review.
findings.effect_size: 21 pigs (9 bleeding-analogy, 12 kidney-transplant); blood-loss thresholds >700 mL=0 to <55 mL=3
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: For the in vivo study, 21 female German landrace pigs have been used either to study bleeding analogy (n = 9) or to apply pSAS after abdominal surgery in a kidney transplant model (n = 12).
findings.study_system: German landrace pigs; surgical Apgar score in laboratory animal science (refinement)

findings.claim: Accounting for intracluster correlation among same-group cage mates in the statistical design lets experiments use more cages with fewer animals, improving power while reducing animal numbers under the 3Rs.
findings.claim_source_sentence: This statistical efficiency, which means more power, can be translated into reduced animal numbers, one of the 3Rs (replace, reduce, refine) of animal research.
findings.evidence: Tutorial on linear mixed models, power and cost analyses for cohoused-animal experiments.
findings.study_system: Statistical methods; intracluster correlation in cage-mate experiments (Reduction)

findings.claim: Blinding and randomisation are core methods for reducing bias in preclinical studies, but require strong protocols and a team approach because incomplete or improper implementation is a recognised source of bias.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Blinding and randomisation are important methods for increasing the robustness of pre-clinical studies, as incomplete or improper implementation thereof is recognised as a source of bias.
findings.evidence: Methodological review with practical guidance on randomisation and blinding in animal studies.
findings.study_system: Methodological review; blinding and randomisation in animal experiments

findings.claim: A 14-year survey of 3768 preclinical urology studies found persistently low reporting of key bias-prevention design elements, with sample-size estimation reported in only 1.0% of studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Randomisation was reported in 50.0%, blinding in 15.0%, sample size estimation in 1.0%, inclusion of both sexes in 6.3%, statistical analysis in 97.1%, housing and husbandry in 47.7%, and inclusion/exclusion criteria in 5.0%.
findings.evidence: Systematic review of study-design elements in preclinical urological research 2007-2021.
findings.effect_size: randomisation 50.0%, blinding 15.0%, sample size estimation 1.0% (of 3768 studies)
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Randomisation was reported in 50.0%, blinding in 15.0%, sample size estimation in 1.0%, inclusion of both sexes in 6.3%, statistical analysis in 97.1%, housing and husbandry in 47.7%, and inclusion/exclusion criteria in 5.0%.
findings.study_system: 3768 preclinical urological animal studies (2007-2021)

findings.claim: Screening 1,277 Swiss applications for animal experiments showed measures against bias were described at very low rates, so licensing authorities lack the information about scientific validity needed for a meaningful harm-benefit analysis.
findings.claim_source_sentence: These results indicate that the authorities licensing animal experiments are lacking important information about experimental conduct that determines the scientific validity of the findings, which may be critical for the weight attributed to the benefit of the research in the harm-benefit analysis.
findings.evidence: Comparison of bias-measure description rates in applications vs resulting publications.
findings.effect_size: bias measures described in 2.4%-19% of applications; 0.0% sample-size calculation in publications; application-publication internal-validity correlation Spearman rho = 0.34, p = 0.014
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Measures against bias were described at very low rates, ranging on average from 2.4% for statistical analysis plan to 19% for primary outcome variable in applications for animal experiments, and from 0.0% for sample size calculation to 34% for statistical analysis plan in publications from these experiments.
findings.study_system: 1,277 Swiss animal-experiment applications + 50 resulting publications

findings.claim: A meta-analysis of animal depression models rated overall reporting quality as only intermediate (ARRIVE ratio 0.63) and found that almost no authors shared underlying data, undermining reproducibility and reuse.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Only 2.35% (5 out of 212) of corresponding authors responded to our data request.
findings.evidence: Systematic review/meta-analysis of 25 antidepressant studies with ARRIVE and SYRCLE assessment.
findings.effect_size: ARRIVE quality ratio 0.63; 2.35% (5 of 212) authors responded to data request
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Only 2.35% (5 out of 212) of corresponding authors responded to our data request.
findings.study_system: 25 preclinical antidepressant/depression-model studies; reporting quality and data availability

findings.claim: A systematic review found that despite the extensive use of zebrafish, evidence on how holding density affects their welfare is scarce, and density should be included in universal housing guidelines and routinely reported.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We stress the necessity of including holding density in universal housing guidelines and reporting information on holding conditions of larvae and adults when publishing zebrafish work.
findings.evidence: Systematic review of publications on zebrafish holding density and welfare indicators.
findings.study_system: Zebrafish; systematic review of holding density and welfare

findings.claim: An expert workshop concluded that the euthanasia methods recommended in Directive 2010/63/EU, derived from food-fish, are either inapplicable or interfere with research goals for zebrafish, requiring species-specific refinement.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Consequently, the currently recommended methods of euthanasia in the Directive 2010/63/EU are either not applicable or may interfere with research goals.
findings.evidence: International workshop white paper proposing alternative zebrafish euthanasia methods.
findings.study_system: Zebrafish; euthanasia methods (workshop white paper)

findings.claim: Directive 2010/63/EU made severity classification (mild, moderate, severe, humane endpoint) of pain and distress in laboratory zebrafish a new and challenging routine task, addressed here with a dedicated welfare score sheet.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The identification and assessment of pain, distress, or harm, according to a severity classification of mild, moderate, severe, or humane endpoint, became a new challenging task for all scientists, animal technicians, and veterinarians for daily work with laboratory zebrafish.
findings.evidence: Development of a welfare score-sheet plus a 3-year survey of colony abnormalities.
findings.study_system: Laboratory zebrafish; welfare score-sheet and severity classification

findings.claim: Because zebrafish embryos are not protected under current EU animal welfare legislation, an embryo-based thyroid-disruption test represents a 3Rs-compatible replacement/reduction alternative to protected-animal tests.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Zebrafish embryos, not protected by current European Union animal welfare legislation, represent a promising model.
findings.evidence: Development of a fish-embryo-toxicity-based test integrating molecular, morphological and behavioural endpoints.
findings.study_system: Zebrafish embryos; thyroid-disruption test (replacement/3Rs ecotoxicology)

findings.claim: In-silico modeling of zebrafish behaviour is proposed as a way to support all three Rs, potentially reducing the very large volume of live zebrafish anxiety experiments.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In-silico experiments could significantly contribute to zebrafish research and welfare, by offering new means to support the 3Rs principles of replacement, reduction, and refinement.
findings.evidence: Data-driven Markov/stochastic modeling of zebrafish response to caffeine.
findings.effect_size: more than 5000 technical zebrafish papers published each year
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Every year, more than 5000 technical papers are published about zebrafish, many of them seeking to explain the underpinnings of anxiety through animal testing.
findings.study_system: Zebrafish behavioural pharmacology; in-silico modeling (3Rs)

findings.claim: Emerging techniques (in vitro cell and organ-on-a-chip systems, model organisms, toxicogenomics) are driving a shift away from animal testing in drug-discovery toxicology, motivated by the 3Rs.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Although animal testing is still considered as the "gold standard" in traditional toxicity testing, there is a necessity for shift from animal testing to alternative methods regarding the drug safety testing owing to the emerging state-of-art techniques and the proposal of 3Rs (replace, reduce, and refine) towards animal welfare.
findings.evidence: Review of new-approach methodologies in drug-discovery toxicology.
findings.study_system: Review; drug-discovery toxicology alternatives (organ-on-chip, model organisms, toxicogenomics)

findings.claim: An updated evidence assessment concluded there is strong evidence of sentience in octopuses and cuttlefish, meeting six of eight neural/behavioural sentience criteria with high confidence, with weaker evidence for squid and unknown status for nautilus.
findings.claim_source_sentence: There is strong evidence of sentience in octopuses and cuttlefish, which are assessed with very high or high confidence in meeting six of eight criteria.
findings.evidence: Eight-criterion neural and behavioural sentience framework applied to cephalopod taxa.
findings.effect_size: octopus/cuttlefish: 6 of 8 criteria high confidence; squid 5 of 8; nautilus 1 of 8
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: There is strong evidence of sentience in octopuses and cuttlefish, which are assessed with very high or high confidence in meeting six of eight criteria.
findings.study_system: Cephalopod molluscs (octopus, cuttlefish, squid, nautilus); sentience assessment (8 criteria)

findings.claim: Extending ethical consideration to echinoderms, the authors propose a broadened 5Rs framework adding 'responsibility' and 'respect' to the 3Rs, while noting invertebrates' presumed non-sentience is what favours them as replacement models.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In this context, we discuss the development of a broader conceptual framework of 5Rs that includes responsibility and respect, which may guide practices ensuring welfare in echinoderms, even in the absence of any particular normative.
findings.evidence: Conceptual paper on echinoderm welfare and an extended Rs framework.
findings.study_system: Echinoderms/invertebrates; ethical framework (5Rs)

findings.claim: Live cephalopods were added to Directive 2010/63/EU because new scientific evidence of their sentience met the fundamental criterion determining which species fall under the Directive's protection.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The inclusion of "live cephalopods" in the Directive 2010/63/EU has been prompted by new scientific knowledge on the "sentience" of animals used for experimental or other scientific purposes, a fundamental criterion to which animal species are included or not under the protective umbrella of the Directive.
findings.evidence: Commentary on EU care-and-welfare guidelines for cephalopods in research.
findings.study_system: Cephalopods; EU Directive 2010/63/EU welfare guidelines

findings.claim: A review of adult fish reproductive toxicity tests found chronically low sample sizes and high variance, so only large effects could be detected; refining study design (timing, duration, more replicate tanks) increased statistical power.
findings.claim_source_sentence: A review conducted of 62 published adult fish reproductive papers using various fish species found low samples sizes (mean of 5.7 replicates with a median of 5 replicates) and high variance (an average coefficient of variance of 43.8%).
findings.evidence: Literature review plus mummichog case study identifying design refinements to increase test power.
findings.effect_size: mean 5.7 replicates (median 5), coefficient of variance 43.8%; average detectable difference was a 68.7% reduction in egg production
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The high variances and low sample sizes allow only relatively large differences to be detected with the current protocols; the average significant difference detected was a 68.7% reduction in egg production, while only differences above 50% were detected with confidence.
findings.study_system: Adult fish reproductive toxicity tests (mummichog, Fundulus heteroclitus); experimental-design refinement

findings.claim: A systematic review and meta-analysis of European scientists' experiences implementing the 3Rs found 91% saw education as beneficial for implementation, yet when asked about their own field researchers did not see replacement as possible, treating refinement as a higher and more achievable priority.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Our meta-analysis showed that 91% of scientists saw education as beneficial for 3Rs implementation (Q18).
findings.evidence: Results/Discussion. 17 publications (8 quantitative, 7 qualitative, 2 mixed) synthesized into eight themes (four barriers, four facilitators); meta-analysis: scientists skeptical about achieving replacement even while believing 3R improve experimental quality.
findings.effect_size: 91% of scientists saw education as beneficial
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Our meta-analysis showed that 91% of scientists saw education as beneficial for 3Rs implementation (Q18).
findings.study_system: systematic review/meta-analysis of European animal researchers' 3R implementation perceptions (17 publications)

findings.claim: A German funding programme ran 17 preclinical studies designed as rigorously planned, multi-laboratory confirmatory experiments to generate robust evidence and reduce failing clinical translation, proposing new roles such as preclinical research coordinators.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In a unique funding call, 17 studies in Germany aimed to confirm exploratory findings across various biomedical research fields in a rigorously planned and executed multi-laboratory set-up.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Meta-research project accompanied the 17 studies to investigate confirmatory design; workshop identified pitfalls and optimization strategies for large-scale academic preclinical research.
findings.effect_size: 17 confirmatory multi-laboratory studies
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In a unique funding call, 17 studies in Germany aimed to confirm exploratory findings across various biomedical research fields in a rigorously planned and executed multi-laboratory set-up.
findings.study_system: preclinical confirmatory multi-laboratory studies (Germany, 17 projects)

findings.claim: The authors argue that 'experimental philosophical bioethics' (bioxphi) should be used to investigate '3R dilemmas' - real conflicts between replacement, reduction and refinement faced by professional animal-research decision makers, who routinely decide the suffering and death of many animals.
findings.claim_source_sentence: For this reason, a context-specific investigation of so-called "3R dilemmas" (i.e., dilemmas where there is a conflict between the principles of replacement, reduction, and refinement of the use of animals in research) is essential to improve the situation of both non-human animals and human stakeholders.
findings.evidence: Abstract/argument. Provides a bioxphi template for 3R dilemmas and recommendations, arguing sacrificial dilemmas are experienced in real life by animal-research decision makers unlike abstract trolley problems.
findings.study_system: animal research ethics decision-making (experimental bioethics methodology)

findings.claim: The authors propose a Benefit Assessment Matrix for animal ethics committees premised on the idea that rigorous high-quality research is more likely to produce benefit than low-rigour research, aiming to rapidly phase out poor-quality animal research.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The organizational premise is that rigorous high-quality research is more likely to produce tangible benefit than poor quality, low rigor research.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Frames a compromise in the animal-research debate accepting that not all research provides enough benefit to justify animal use; matrix guides scientists and IACUC/AEC benefit assessment.
findings.study_system: animal research ethics review / harm-benefit (proposed Benefit Assessment Matrix tool)

findings.claim: Across ten mouse datasets spanning three models, body weight and clinical distress score outperformed burrowing and nesting as distress indicators; discriminatory power depended strongly on distress severity, with excellent discrimination (AUC >= 0.91) only in acute high-distress phases.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Across all three animal models and distress levels, body weight and the distress score showed higher discriminative performance and better accuracy than burrowing activity or nesting behavior.
findings.evidence: Results/Discussion (fulltext). ROC analyses across transmitter implantation, bile duct ligation and chronic pancreatitis; under low distress, burrowing accuracy fell to 39-88% and nesting to 19-56%; cut-offs derived in mild-distress settings did not transfer across projects.
findings.effect_size: AUC >= 0.91 in acute high-distress phase; nesting accuracy as low as 19% under low distress
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Body weight change, the distress score, burrowing, and nesting behavior showed excellent discriminative ability, with AUC ≥ 0.91 when exploring the acute phase after transmitter implantation.
findings.study_system: laboratory mice, ten datasets (transmitter implantation, bile duct ligation, chronic pancreatitis)

findings.claim: The first longitudinal (2-year, five-organization) trial of institutional compassion-fatigue resiliency programs found no significant change in professional quality of life, job retention or satisfaction, though participants' understanding of coping strategies increased.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Therefore, there is a gap in the long-term evaluation of compassion fatigue resiliency programs for personnel that work with animals in research.
findings.evidence: Results (fulltext). Pre-post trial in five USA/Canada organizations; hypothesized improvement in professional quality of life, satisfaction and retention was not observed; quality of life remained associated with satisfaction and retention.
findings.effect_size: no significant change over 2 years (negative result)
findings.study_system: laboratory animal personnel across five organizations (2-year pre-post longitudinal trial)

findings.claim: Qualitative interviews across management, science, regulation and care groups found that 'animal agency' plays a subordinate role in the culture of care, and that strategies are implemented in everyday practice to largely fade out animals' agency.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Overall, the results of the qualitative survey showed that animal agency plays a subordinate role in the question of a culture of care in animal research.
findings.evidence: Results/Conclusion. Guideline-based expert interviews; animal agency appears in the theoretical reception of culture of care but is not established in practice.
findings.study_system: qualitative expert interviews, laboratory animal science professionals

findings.claim: An industry working group developed a Culture of Care framework identifying five focus areas but cautioned it must not be used as an auditing/tick-box tool, only as a starting point for reflection within each establishment's constraints.
findings.claim_source_sentence: To prevent it supporting a 'tick-box' exercise, the framework must not be used as an auditing tool, but as a starting point for consideration and discussion about how care manifests within the context and constraints of individual establishments.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Framework covers company values, strategic approach, implementation structures, staff support, and animal care and procedures; notes 'Culture of Care' is used widely but rarely with defined indicators.
findings.effect_size: five areas of focus
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The framework is a tool that identifies five areas of focus for a Culture of Care: company values; strategic approach at establishment level; implementation structures; staff support; and animal care and procedures.
findings.study_system: European pharmaceutical industry animal research (Culture of Care framework)

findings.claim: A comparative overview of non-human primate neuroimaging welfare standards across nations proposes an International Animal Welfare and Use Committee and argues that transparent promotion of care, welfare and research impact may reduce public concern about animal experiments in neuroscience.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The transparent promotion of this level of care and welfare, along with the results of the research and its impact, may reduce public concerns associated with animal experiments in neuroscience research.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Focuses on marmoset and macaque neuroimaging research; compares ethics/regulations to build a common welfare standard and international guidelines.
findings.study_system: non-human primate (marmoset, macaque) neuroimaging research regulation (international comparison)

findings.claim: A national study found no prior literature had quantified UK laboratory-animal rehoming; rehoming can both improve and compromise welfare and addresses the arguably unnecessary killing of some animals after procedures.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Indeed, despite the widely recognised benefits to rehoming, and concerns surrounding the routine nature of killing within animal research facilities, no literature quantifies how many animals are rehomed from UK laboratories.
findings.evidence: Introduction/Discussion (fulltext). Survey of 41 of ~160 UK facilities (25% response); rehoming occurs routinely but numbers small; primary motivation is staff morale and a positive ethical profile.
findings.study_system: UK laboratory animal rehoming practices (national survey, 41 facilities)

findings.claim: A concept paper argues that most currently-used culture-of-care indicators are human-centric and subjective, and recommends supplementing them with objective, animal-centric criteria assessed separately for each of the 3Rs.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Many currently-used criteria and indicators tend to be human-centric and subjective, and we suggest using further objective indicators and animal-centric, 3Rs-based criteria.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Reviews surrogate measures and surveys used to assess culture of care; recommends UK/EU regulator documents as sources of objective indicators.
findings.study_system: culture of care assessment (concept paper)
