findings.claim: Developing an epistemology of 'speciesist ignorance', the author argues humans as a privileged group can comfortably remain ignorant of their participation in collective wrongdoing toward animals, which sustains speciesism and obstructs reform.
findings.claim_source_sentence: I argue that humans, taken as a group, enjoy a position of privilege, which allows them to comfortably remain ignorant of their participation in collective wrongdoings towards animals.
findings.evidence: Abstract/argument. Extends the epistemology of ignorance (racism, sexism) to speciesism; distinguishes individual and group-based accounts of speciesist ignorance.
findings.study_system: animal ethics / social epistemology of ignorance (philosophy)

findings.claim: An ethnographic study of UK junior animal technicians argues that care and harm coexist: caring practices are enacted alongside the permitted harms inflicted on research animals and the harms suffered by technicians in the processes of caring for and killing animals.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We propose that different notions of care are enacted alongside, not only permitted levels of harm inflicted on research animals following research protocols, but also harms to ATs in the processes of caring and killing animals.
findings.evidence: Analysis. Longitudinal ethnography and interviews 2013-2015 examining skills, prior care experience, institutional/affective environments and experiences of killing.
findings.study_system: UK laboratory animal technicians (ethnography, 2013-2015)

findings.claim: A web-based Critical Incident Reporting System for laboratory animal science (CIRS-LAS) was created to share failures and support reduction and refinement, but uptake was modest (303 members, 52 reports), showing an open error culture is difficult to establish.
findings.claim_source_sentence: CIRS-LAS is open to all individuals working with laboratory animals worldwide and currently exists with 303 registered members, 52 reports, and an average of 71 visitors per month.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Reporting system addresses reduction/refinement by preventing repetition of failed experiments; negative experiences are often unpublished due to fear of hostility.
findings.effect_size: 303 registered members, 52 reports, 71 visitors/month
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: CIRS-LAS is open to all individuals working with laboratory animals worldwide and currently exists with 303 registered members, 52 reports, and an average of 71 visitors per month.
findings.study_system: laboratory animal science critical-incident reporting system (CIRS-LAS)

findings.claim: On utility-maximization grounds, the author argues that animal models should be phased out of neuropsychiatric research because leading theories of the human mind invoke sociocultural factors not homologized in nonhuman animals, so the expected epistemic/clinical benefits are doubtful.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The author argues on utility maximization grounds that we should phase out animal models in neuropsychiatric research.
findings.evidence: Abstract/argument. Challenges the standard cost-benefit justification for animal models of depression, anxiety and schizophrenia.
findings.study_system: animal models of mental disorders (philosophy/ethics)

findings.claim: A narrative review argues that ethological needs conserved after domestication mean standard laboratory housing generates chronic stress and systematic bias, so housing conditions should be treated as integral experimental-design variables rather than secondary technical details.
findings.claim_source_sentence: As a result, standard laboratory housing may generate chronic stress, alter behavior, and introduce systematic bias into experimental data.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Problem-oriented review of social housing, enrichment, temperature and lighting; links refinement to reproducibility and translational validity in mice.
findings.study_system: laboratory mice housing/welfare (narrative review)

findings.claim: Two culture-of-care training initiatives - a 'Care-full Stories' storytelling tool and research-integrity/culture-of-care training for low- and middle-income communities - are reflected on as ways to create safe spaces for laboratory animal professionals to discuss emotions and caring responsibilities.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Firstly, the 'Care-full Stories' tool, which uses fictionalised prompts (storytelling) to encourage participants to share their own stories from working in animal research.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Argues culture of care must be integrated into education with reflective learning; delivery method and locality are key to uptake and sustainability.
findings.study_system: laboratory animal professionals training (culture of care education)

findings.claim: Proposing a foundation for animal research ethics as a field, the authors map seven phases of animal experiments and identify 16 key ethical, legal and practical challenges plus four meta-challenges (moral pluralism, integrating outside views, international plurality, interdisciplinary education).
findings.claim_source_sentence: In total, 16 key ethical, legal, and practical challenges that an ethical framework for the use of animals in research needs to address are identified and analyzed.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Interdisciplinary/international framing spanning research ethics, animal ethics, scientific and legal aspects.
findings.effect_size: seven phases; 16 key challenges; four meta-challenges
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: In total, 16 key ethical, legal, and practical challenges that an ethical framework for the use of animals in research needs to address are identified and analyzed.
findings.study_system: animal research ethics framework (interdisciplinary)

findings.claim: Critically examining animal experimentation in translational research on epistemological and ethical grounds, the authors advocate a paradigm shift to new approach methodologies (NAMs) as complete replacements, arguing replacement should be prioritized over all other considerations.
findings.claim_source_sentence: In this context, replacement emerges as the key principle-an imperative that should be prioritized over all other considerations.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Grounds the duty to protect animals in the intrinsic value of their well-being, not just instrumental value; targets cancer and complex-disease models.
findings.study_system: preclinical/translational animal research (critical epistemological-ethical analysis)

findings.claim: An editorial review of US IACUCs argues structural limitations undermine review quality - members need no subject-matter expertise, need not verify non-duplication, and most institutions now allow single-member (Designated Member Review) approval - so IACUC approval should not be treated as evidence of ethical adherence.
findings.claim_source_sentence: The majority of U.S. research institutions now allow research proposals to be approved by a single committee member, using a system called Designated Member Review, without full committee consideration.
findings.evidence: Results/Conclusions. Contrasts US 'consider alternatives' with EU mandatory harm-benefit and required use of alternatives; recommends expert reviewers and mandatory non-animal searches.
findings.study_system: US Institutional Animal Care and Use Committees (editorial review)

findings.claim: Reviewing psychological evidence, the authors argue folk morality is 'deontological all the way down' (Multi-level Weighted Deontology) - the side-constraints protecting animals are much weaker than those protecting humans - undercutting the assumption that people are utilitarian about animals.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We review evidence suggesting that the folk is deontological all the way down-it is just that the moral side constraints that protect animals from harm are much weaker than those that protect humans.
findings.evidence: Abstract/review. Challenges the Nozickian Hybrid View (deontology for humans, utilitarianism for animals); notes species-membership factors shape intuitions about human moral status.
findings.study_system: moral psychology of animal moral status (review of empirical studies)

findings.claim: A legal-ethical analysis argues the Swiss animal-dignity law paradoxically undermines dignity, functioning to ensure animals can be used merely as a means, and concludes the Swiss Animal Welfare Act is deeply unethical.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We conclude that previous criticisms of the law do not go far enough: far from protecting animal dignity, the Swiss law not only undermines such dignity but itself serves as a means to ensure that animals can be used merely as a means, and not treated with respect.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Analyses Swiss constitutional requirement to treat animals with dignity and the Animal Welfare Act implementing it.
findings.study_system: Swiss animal-dignity legislation (legal/ethical analysis)

findings.claim: Interviews with 15 physicians experienced in 'live tissue training' (using live anaesthetised animals) revealed predominantly consequentialist justifications (human life valued above animal life; no adequate alternative), with the 3Rs invoked both to restrict and to defend their involvement.
findings.claim_source_sentence: There is a predominant consequentialist thinking regarding the use of live animals, with evidence that the 3Rs principles are being considered, if not explicitly, as a restriction on the use of animals for LTT and also partly to justify or defend medical professionals' involvement.
findings.evidence: Results/Conclusion. Fifteen semi-structured interviews; live tissue training contested yet continues despite simulator alternatives; professional identity and speciesism shape justifications.
findings.effect_size: 15 semi-structured interviews
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Fifteen semi-structured interviews of physicians who had knowledge and prior experience of LTT were performed as part of a wider research project and initially analysed using the Framework Method.
findings.study_system: physicians who participated in live tissue training (qualitative interviews)

findings.claim: A survey of 653 Spanish university students found most support animal use in research, but attitudes were strongly shaped by species - companion animals drew most opposition while rodents, invertebrates and aquatic species received highest support - and anthropomorphism was negatively correlated with support.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Species strongly influenced attitudes: companion animals generated the most opposition, primates and livestock elicited mixed responses, and rodents, invertebrates, and aquatic species received the highest support.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Attitudes differed by gender and field of study (men and science students more accepting); only anthropomorphism showed moderate negative correlation with support.
findings.effect_size: n=653 students
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: The sample included 653 students, predominantly women, heterosexual, and urban residents.
findings.study_system: Spanish university students' attitudes to animal use (survey)

findings.claim: A 3Rs review of experimental liver disease research maintains that animal models remain essential for understanding the pathogenesis and progression of human liver disease, while summarizing techniques to replace, reduce and refine such studies.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Experimentation in animal models is essential to understand the pathogenesis of human diseases and, considering the high prevalence of liver disease worldwide, to understand the pathophysiology of disease progression and the molecular pathways involved, due to the complexity of the liver as an organ and its relationship with the rest of the organism.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Comprehensive summary of replace/reduce/refine techniques and advantages/weaknesses of experimental liver-disease models.
findings.study_system: experimental liver disease animal models (3Rs review)

findings.claim: Qualitative research on rehoming, veterinary clinical research and the Named Veterinary Surgeon role shows the ethical, affective and practical elements of care are split in the research laboratory, and that animal categories are flexible and context-dependent.
findings.claim_source_sentence: We begin by exploring how (in theory and practice) the ethical, affective, and practical elements of care are split in the research laboratory.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Examines decisions to end or extend animal life through clinical research and rehoming, surfacing norms and dilemmas around animal death in laboratory and clinic.
findings.study_system: UK animal research rehoming and veterinary care (qualitative research)

findings.claim: A UK case study on rat cage height found the Code of Practice permits 20 cm cages although adult rats rear to 30 cm, so most cannot stand upright; barriers to higher caging are largely non-scientific (financial, health-and-safety, human) and supporting evidence already exists.
findings.claim_source_sentence: Within this, the Code of Practice currently allows laboratory rats to be housed in cages that are 20 cm high, even though adults can rear up to 30 cm.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Barriers grouped into health-and-safety, financial, animal-welfare, scientific and 'human'; recommends education and access to existing evidence rather than new evidence.
findings.effect_size: 20 cm cages vs 30 cm rearing height
findings.effect_size_source_sentence: Within this, the Code of Practice currently allows laboratory rats to be housed in cages that are 20 cm high, even though adults can rear up to 30 cm.
findings.study_system: laboratory rats housing/refinement (UK case study)

findings.claim: A historical analysis argues the 3Rs' founding text (Russell and Burch, 1959) remains little-read because its synthesis of humanistic and scientific values fell across C. P. Snow's 'two cultures' divide, and that the humanities and social sciences can still improve animal research.
findings.claim_source_sentence: By adopting a historical perspective, this article argues that one explanation for this disjunction may be found in another, more celebrated, event of 1959: C. P. Snow's Rede lecture on The Two Cultures.
findings.evidence: Abstract. Notes muted early scientific interest in the 3Rs and that the original text remains out of print and little read despite the 3Rs' later success.
findings.study_system: history of the 3Rs / Russell and Burch (historical analysis)

establishing.thesis: The 3Rs (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) are the ethical and legal architecture of animal research, yet they are systematically under-implemented and are increasingly argued to be insufficient without a scientific-value/reporting dimension. This section introduces 'data welfare': the claim that complete reporting, FAIR stewardship and reuse of animal-derived data extend Reduction and Refinement, so wasting data is a welfare failure the 3Rs should already forbid.
establishing.synthesis: Data welfare is only actionable if data can actually be made reusable; sec-fair-preclinical tests whether the FAIR principles - the leading operationalisation of data welfare - deliver reuse in practice.

complication.thesis: The 3Rs (Replacement, Reduction, Refinement) are the ethical and legal architecture of animal research, yet they are systematically under-implemented and are increasingly argued to be insufficient without a scientific-value/reporting dimension. conflicts.paper_a_claim: Given these caveats of HBA, I call policy-makers to reconsider the place of HBA in animal research.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Ultimately, we argue that the two models are not mutually exclusive and may be combined to make the most of their advantages while reducing the disadvantages of how harm-benefit analysis in typically undertaken.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether project-level harm-benefit analysis should be abandoned and replaced by independent harm-minimisation principles (Gutfreund) or retained and improved by combining discourse and metric weighting models (Grimm, Olsson & Sandoe).

conflicts.paper_a_claim: However, animal welfare alone does not suffice to make animal research ethical if the research does not have sufficient scientific value.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: It is not always possible to apply the Principle in all of its three aspects, but this does not absolutely mean that the Principle as an idea is neither obsolete nor ineffective.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether the classic 3Rs framework is inadequate and must be expanded with scientific-value principles (Strech & Dirnagl's 6Rs) or remains conceptually sufficient and merely under-applied (Vitale & Ricceri).

conflicts.paper_a_claim: First, we criticise some justifications for the claim that human beings and more complex animals have higher moral status.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Such an examination demonstrates, I believe, that the practical implications of leading theories converge far more than might be expected.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether graded moral status by cognitive complexity is philosophically defensible (challenged by Bovenkerk & Kaldewaij) or whether competing moral-status theories nonetheless converge enough to guide practice (DeGrazia).

conflicts.paper_a_claim: A careful analysis of indicative primate blood markers for chronic inflammation, hydration status, and stress levels, their comparison to baseline values from both the same animals and the literature, and evaluation of additional hematologic, physiological, and behavioral parameters did not provide support for the notion of long-term, cumulative effects on the monkeys' healthiness and well-being.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: I propose that telomere attrition, a cellular biomarker of biological age, provides a molecular measure of cumulative experience that could be used to assess the welfare impact of husbandry regimes and/or experimental procedures on non-human animals.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether repeated 'mildly severe' laboratory procedures produce measurable long-term cumulative harm: an NHP blood-marker dataset detects none, whereas the telomere-attrition framework predicts cumulative physiological damage that conventional markers may miss.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: In general, scenarios involving chronic pain in mice, organ transplantation in pigs and skin cancer in fish all exhibited higher levels of support than what is typically reported for animal research [,].
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Expectations for AR are much higher than empirical data show to have been achieved.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether public attitudes to animal research are more supportive than commonly assumed (specific protocols attract higher-than-typical support) or fundamentally fragile because they rest on unmet expectations of methodological quality and human translation.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: A harm-benefit analysis can be used to weigh the welfare and quality of life of animals in scientific studies against the resulting benefits to other animals or humans, provided that animal welfare can be validly assessed.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: The argument above that HBA in IACUC discussions may result in a bias against basic research is not a mere theoretical concern.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether project-level harm-benefit analysis is a valid and usable tool for weighing animal welfare against benefits (Wolfensohn et al.) or is structurally biased against basic research and should be replaced by independent principles (Gutfreund).

conflicts.paper_a_claim: In all groups, the vast majority of participants were able to recognise stress in laboratory animals.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: The examples of severity classification given in Annex VIII are limited in number, and have little descriptive power to aid assignment.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: How reliably procedure severity can be assigned in practice: a training study finds most personnel can recognise and grade stress after instruction, whereas the FELASA working group finds the regulatory severity framework too underspecified to support consistent assignment.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: The rise in catecholamine concentrations suggests that CO2 exposure might be linked to a higher stress response compared to isoflurane and sevoflurane exposure, although we did not observe a behavioral correlate for that.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: CO2 (0.9 ± 0.18) and isoflurane (1.2 ± 0.20) recorded the highest scores
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether volatile inhalant anaesthetics are a genuine welfare refinement over CO2 for rodent euthanasia: a mouse blood-catecholamine study finds CO2 more stressful than isoflurane/sevoflurane, whereas a Rat Grimace Scale study finds isoflurane produces the highest facial pain scores of the agents tested.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: Decision-making based on deliberation among committee members should be supported over the use of scoring approaches.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: A harm-benefit analysis can be used to weigh the welfare and quality of life of animals in scientific studies against the resulting benefits to other animals or humans, provided that animal welfare can be validly assessed.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether harm-benefit analysis should rely on deliberative, case-by-case committee judgement (scoping review favours deliberation over scoring) or on validated quantitative welfare-scoring tools (Wolfensohn et al.'s AWAG approach), i.e. deliberation versus metric scoring as the more valid basis for HBA.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: This study develops a composite HBA method composed of the relevant and useful elements from current guidance documents and provides instructions on conducting such an analysis.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: The argument above that HBA in IACUC discussions may result in a bias against basic research is not a mere theoretical concern.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether project-level harm-benefit analysis can be operationalised into a coherent, workable decision tool (compound model) or is inherently biased against basic research and should be replaced by two independent principles (societal benefit; minimal justified harm).

conflicts.paper_a_claim: Although heterogenization significantly increased within-experiment variation relative to between-experiment variation, the effect was too weak to account for the large variation between laboratories and improve reproducibility substantially.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: By contrast, multi-laboratory designs including as few as 2 to 4 laboratories increased coverage probability by up to 42 percentage points without a need for larger sample sizes.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: An empirical six-laboratory test found simple within-study heterogenization too weak to overcome between-laboratory variation, whereas a simulation across 440 studies concludes that multi-laboratory designs with only 2-4 labs substantially improve reproducibility of effect-size estimates; they disagree on how effective heterogenization/multi-lab strategies are for solving poor reproducibility.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: As invertebrates are generally classified as non-sentient animals, the replacement dimension tends to favor them as prevalent models in experimental research.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: There is strong evidence of sentience in octopuses and cuttlefish, which are assessed with very high or high confidence in meeting six of eight criteria.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: One framework treats invertebrates as generally non-sentient, making them preferred 'replacement' models under the 3Rs, while the cephalopod assessment finds strong evidence of sentience in some invertebrates (octopus, cuttlefish), undercutting the assumption that invertebrate use is ethically low-cost replacement.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: Neither the overall score nor any individual parameter yielded satisfactory results for predicting survival.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: This finding provides first evidence that nest scoring might serve as a simple and valid approach to evaluate rat well-being during routine assessment schemes.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: In a rat surgery/cirrhosis model, standard severity score-sheet parameters were found insufficient to predict mortality, whereas a rat kindling study concludes that a single simple measure (nest scoring) is a valid approach to assess well-being; they disagree on how reliably simple welfare scores capture severity.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: In this context, replacement emerges as the key principle-an imperative that should be prioritized over all other considerations.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Experimentation in animal models is essential to understand the pathogenesis of human diseases and, considering the high prevalence of liver disease worldwide, to understand the pathophysiology of disease progression and the molecular pathways involved, due to the complexity of the liver as an organ and its relationship with the rest of the organism.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether new approach methodologies can and should completely replace animals now (replacement as an overriding imperative) versus the position that animal models remain essential for understanding complex human-disease pathogenesis and progression.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: More specifically, we describe a Benefit Assessment Matrix that can provide a streamlined and practical guide for both scientists and Animal Ethics Committees or equivalent bodies such as Institutional Animal Care and Use Committees to assess the benefit of proposed research.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: The argument above that HBA in IACUC discussions may result in a bias against basic research is not a mere theoretical concern.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether ethics committees should formally assess the benefit of proposed animal research (a Benefit Assessment Matrix to phase out low-value work) versus the position that benefit/harm-benefit assessment biases committees against basic research and should be replaced by independent principles.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: To prevent it supporting a 'tick-box' exercise, the framework must not be used as an auditing tool, but as a starting point for consideration and discussion about how care manifests within the context and constraints of individual establishments.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Many currently-used criteria and indicators tend to be human-centric and subjective, and we suggest using further objective indicators and animal-centric, 3Rs-based criteria.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: How to assess culture of care: caution against objective auditing/benchmarking that risks becoming a tick-box exercise versus advocacy for more objective, measurable animal-centric 3Rs-based indicators and benchmarking.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: No manuscript in either group achieved full compliance with the ARRIVE checklist.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: There was an improvement in the reporting of risks of bias in in vivo research in NPG journals following a change in editorial policy, to a level that to our knowledge has not been previously observed.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether journal checklist interventions improve reporting of animal research. IICARus (a randomised trial requesting ARRIVE-checklist completion at submission to PLOS ONE) found no improvement in full ARRIVE compliance, whereas NPQIP found a mandatory Nature checklist at revision raised full 'Landis 4' compliance from 0% to 16.4%. They differ on enforcement (voluntary request vs mandatory), outcome definition (full 108-item ARRIVE vs 4 bias items) and journal.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: Unfortunately, publication of ARRIVE guidelines did not seem to enhance reporting quality, compared to papers appeared before ARRIVE publication.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: We find that reporting of randomization, blinding, and sample-size estimation significantly improved when comparing Nature to Cell from 2013 to 2015, likely due to implementation of a checklist.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether ARRIVE/checklists improve reporting. The Chagas review found passive publication of ARRIVE did not improve reporting, while the Nature-vs-Cell study attributed significant improvement to an enforced submission checklist. The divergence maps onto passive dissemination versus active journal enforcement.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: Between 1997 and 2020 (where data were readily available in our data set), rigor and transparency measures showed general improvement (RTI 2.29 to 4.13), suggesting that authors are taking the need for improved reporting seriously.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Reporting quality analysis of preclinical studies revealed substantial reporting deficits across all leading journals, with little improvement over the last 20 years, especially for group size calculations, defining primary versus secondary outcomes, and blinded analysis.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether reporting quality of biomedical/preclinical research has improved over roughly two decades. A large automated cross-field metric (Rigor and Transparency Index over >2M papers) detects a general upward trend, whereas a domain-specific manual audit of kidney preclinical studies finds little improvement over 20 years. The divergence maps onto measurement scope and method (whole-literature automated keyword-based scoring vs deep manual scoring of specific design items) and on field.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: 96.5% of research manuscripts appeared to have provided data- and/or code via link or supplementary material
conflicts.paper_b_claim: A study analyzing 7,750 biomedical research papers published between 2015 and 2020 found that only 9% of all papers pledged to make their data publicly available, and a mere 3% of the total followed through with this commitment.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether data-availability policies translate into actual data sharing: enforced mandatory data/code-sharing policies with editorial checks achieve near-universal (96.5%) provision, whereas voluntary data-availability-statement regimes yield only 3-7% of authors actually sharing usable data. The disagreement is on policy effectiveness and is explained by enforcement mechanism (mandatory-at-review vs voluntary statement).

conflicts.paper_a_claim: The fraction of publications that share all relevant data increased significantly, from 7% in 2014 to 45% in 2023.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Meta-analyses showed a prevalence of declared and actual public data availability of 8% (95% confidence interval 5% to 11%) and 2% (1% to 3%), respectively, between 2016 and 2021.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether research data sharing is substantially improving. A single-institution manual audit (University of Edinburgh biosciences) finds a strong rise to 45% of papers sharing all relevant data by 2023, whereas a field-wide IPD meta-analysis of medical/health research finds actual public data availability stuck at ~2%. The divergence maps onto scope (one progressive institution vs whole literature) and metric definition ('all relevant data' incl. supplementary/genomic deposits vs verified reusable public availability).

conflicts.paper_a_claim: The organizational premise is that rigorous high-quality research is more likely to produce tangible benefit than poor quality, low rigor research.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Because of the limitations of the review process, funding institutions and scientific journals should not use Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee approval of submissions as evidence of adherence to ethical guidelines beyond those legally required.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether ethics-committee/IACUC review can be trusted to safeguard the scientific quality (and hence benefit) of animal research. One proposes a Benefit Assessment Matrix presuming committees can and should assess research rigor/benefit; the other argues US IACUCs structurally lack the expertise and mandate to judge scientific merit, so their approval should not be taken as evidence of ethical adherence. The disagreement is on the feasibility of quality/benefit judgement within existing oversight bodies.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: Before badges, less than 3% of Psychological Science articles reported open data.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: We found that 87.9% of the included studies reported suboptimal adherence to reporting guidelines.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Efficacy of transparency interventions: an enforced, incentivised journal signal (open-practice badges) produced an order-of-magnitude jump in open-data sharing at one journal, whereas two decades of voluntary reporting-guideline availability left ~88% of the literature with suboptimal adherence - implying guideline existence alone is far weaker than enforced incentives.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: Insufficient evidence exists to determine the relation between journals' endorsement of reporting guidelines and the completeness of reporting of published health research reports.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Information about ethical statement and 3R's Principles Before ARRIVE guidelines became widely available, approximately 51% of papers on animal models evaluating drugs for Chagas disease included a statement about compliance with local or international guidelines for experimentation with animals.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether journal endorsement/publication of reporting guidelines improves reporting: a systematic review finds insufficient evidence that endorsement is linked to completeness, while a before/after ARRIVE study finds guideline publication produced no significant improvement (51%->66%, p=0.26) - both undercut the assumption that endorsement drives better reporting but disagree on whether any endorsement-completeness signal exists at all.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: We studied 1,207 institutions from across the world, and found that, in 2017, the top-performing universities published around 80-90% of their research open access.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Over 60% of Tunisian publications remain behind paywalls, limiting their visibility and impact.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Effectiveness/reach of open-access policies is starkly uneven by context: high-income top-performing institutions approach near-universal OA (80-90%), whereas a low-resource national system (Tunisia) remains majority paywalled (>60%), driven by APC/funding barriers.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: The proportion of research outputs published in open access journals or made available on other freely-accessible platforms has increased over the past two decades, driven largely by funder mandates, institutional policies, grass-roots advocacy, and changing attitudes in the research community.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Our findings revealed a modest increase of OS over time but no significant difference between departments with more or less-established OS practices.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Whether institutional/policy interventions effectively raise open-research uptake: OA publishing shows strong mandate/repository-driven growth, but preregistration/data-sharing open-science practices in PhD theses rose only modestly and were unaffected by departmental OS implementation - so policy effect appears practice-specific.

conflicts.paper_a_claim: Multivariable analysis found that novel experimental treatment (OR, 4.64; 95% CI, 0.98-22.02) and funding only from nonprofit sources only (OR, 5.20; 95% CI, 1.21-22.29) were associated with spin.
conflicts.paper_b_claim: Spin was frequent in abstracts (78.9%) and discussions (79.6%), with the highest rates also observed in privately funded (95.7%) and pharmacologic (100%) studies.
conflicts.nature_of_conflict: Opposite direction of the funding-source/spin association: the oncology study links spin to nonprofit funding, whereas the arthroplasty study finds the highest spin rates in privately/industry-funded studies.
